industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral. Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): the rate mechanism that set Construction contractors (M.6) and Cement and aggregates (M.10) at D last week reaches building products this week with a number: Goldman Sachs (13-Oct) estimate each 100 basis points of higher rates cuts developed-market housing investment 6%, Norway's Entra posted a large valuation loss, and construction customers were already postponing investment in last week's read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: D now, D prior, agrees. Counter-case: 26 stocks of mixed character, energy-efficiency retrofit demand benefits from the energy shock, British Land beat with 3 to 5% rental growth guidance, and rate-sensitive groups are where a relief rally starts; no MI Pool name sits in this row. Back to C if the Fed path is marked down.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium on the park and low on any directional view. Signify (LIGHT-NL) is a self-help case at a trough price that has not yet become a recovery case: the 'Modal return' on our modal path is 13.2 percent a year over eighteen months and 12.4 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. The framework's gate line applies and the record does not argue against it: management ('No mediocre management', RA 3, E 1, BB 4) is D and business quality ('Business', E 2, BB 2) is D; predictability ('Transmission', RA 8, E 2, BB 4) and trackability ('Leading indicators', RA 7, E 2, BB 4) are C and pass. Re-open after the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-23. Two re-opening routes are named: a rebased FY2026 range with the Consumer margin above 5 percent and price-cost at or above zero makes the case a 'Trough on Trough' candidate at a price nearer EUR 12, which is where the modal path clears the bar; a held range with an adjusted EBITA margin at or above 8 percent makes it a 'Major Corporate Change' with its first output, and the record would re-open at 'Investment Thesis' C. The case becomes compelling at a price below about EUR 12 or after a guidance rebase that resets the base the recovery is measured from.
case: - The thesis as tested: a new external chief executive has cut the dividend by about 40 percent, suspended the buyback, launched a EUR 180 million indirect-cost programme (900 roles, ahead of schedule, labour consultations completed) and split the portfolio into Build and Harvest, aiming at a circa 10 percent adjusted EBITA margin by 2029 from 8.9 percent in 2025 and 6.1 percent in Q2 2026; at 6.8x the shares re-rate as that happens. The record tests that and finds it not yet material.

- Change Forces (E 1, BB 1, D). External forces (RA 1, D) are strong, new or intensifying and in the wrong direction: competition F (Chinese makers at 50 to 60 percent utilisation redirected into Europe by US tariffs; net price-cost minus 90 basis points in Q2 2026, minus 150 in late 2025; copies 30 percent cheaper; 33 percent of Signify's sales in Europe against under 5 percent of Acuity's); demand D (European permits minus 15 percent in 2024 and falling into 2025; Conventional revenue EUR 1,159 million in FY2019 to EUR 327 million in FY2025; retrofit visibility real but not in any order book); own cycle D (the consensus turn to flat is two years out); supply side D (copper plus 32 percent to USD 13,303 a tonne, silver plus 23 percent, chip shortages at Klite); macro D (rates push construction recovery to 2027 and 2028; euro strength took 7.0 percent off Q1 sales and 4.8 percent off first-half sales; payables exposure EUR 793 million against receivables EUR 402 million); disruption D (connected lighting is the defence, adoption slow, Matter lowers the barrier both ways); regulatory C (the only tailwind, dated 2027 to 2030; tariffs on 31 percent of sales); catch-all D (two OEM customers lost; Acuity's OSRAM digital purchase). Internal forces (RA 2, C): chief executive B, strategy B, standards B meet the three-strong rule; guidance F (cut at Q3 2025, set lower in January 2026, 2029 targets below history); balance sheet F and shareholder returns F (both cut); price rises D (latent and increasingly noted, below cost inflation); other leaders C (bench thinned); new products C; perimeter D, acquisitions D, geographies D, catch-all D. Red-flag check: "PowerPoint transformation" partly (0 to 1 percent growth target; "no spark yet"); the rest no. Propagation: inputs only; 40 basis points of savings showed in Q2 2026.

- Financial Outputs (E 2, BB 1, F). Sell-side upgrades (RA 1, F): our FY2026 EUR 1.60 below guidance (a 7.5 percent floor needs about EUR 246 million in the second half, about 60 percent of the year, done once in five years); guidance above consensus only because consensus disbelieves it (KQ 2, D); the record is misses in FY2023 to FY2025 and a 16 percent Q4 2025 miss (KQ 3, F); the skew is all cuts, Morgan Stanley cutting again by 6.2, 7.1 and 5.2 percent on 2026-10-06 (KQ 4, F); dashboard revisions negative on every line (KQ 5, F); the sell-side calls guidance "already looking stretched" and "highly risky" (KQ 6, F). Key metrics (RA 2, D): margin D (down in six months, 7.9 percent at eighteen on our path, above FY2025 only by 2028), revenue D (very negative to flat), net debt D (rising), cash conversion C (already high and stable). Goldilocks (RA 3, D): six months F (minus 30 percent), eighteen months C (plus 17.5 percent on our path, recovery arithmetic from a base 22 percent below FY2025), three years D (minus 4.7 percent a year from FY2025; 7.1 percent a year forward-to-forward). Staircase (RA 4, D): the dated events are tests the company can fail (Q3 2026, full-year results January 2027) or exogenous steps already discussed (the programme's run-rate, the May 2027 bond, Minamata 2027, the 2030 milestones).
counter_case: Signify is a 'Trough on Trough' already, and the park pays for the trough twice. The price is at a 52-week low after a 34 percent fall; the multiple is 6.8x, the lowest in its sector and the 17th percentile of ten years; 38 percent of the sell-side says sell and only 8 percent buy; estimates are down 37 to 46 percent in a year; and the FY2026 guidance set in January 2026 was the kitchen-sink, because Morgan Stanley's note of 2026-01-30 said it implied 12 to 25 percent EBITA downgrades; the sell-side has done the capitulating since. The business has already right-sized: headcount down about 20 percent since end-2023, Conventional on three plants and back at an 18 percent margin in Q2 2026. The cost programme is ahead of schedule with its benefits concentrated in the second half, after union consultations that closed only in the second quarter, so the second half is structurally better than the first. Retailer stock of Hue is back to 8 to 10 weeks, on or below normal by management's measure, so Consumer sell-in inflects in Q3; underlying sell-out is healthy and the installed base of 175 million light points is growing. Price/mix turned positive for the first time since Q3 2022; Q2 carried one-off plant-consolidation costs. Free cash flow was EUR 268 million in FY2025 on FactSet's definition, 15 percent of the EUR 1,778 million market capitalisation, with consensus at EUR 289 million for FY2026 (16 percent). If the second half delivers the 7.5 percent floor, FY2027 earnings per share of about EUR 2.0 to 2.5 (ING has EUR 2.54) at the ten-year median of 8.4x is EUR 17 to 21 plus a 6 percent yield: 25 to 30 percent a year. The dividend has been reset so it cannot disappoint again; the downside is a stock already at 6.8x. At Building Block level the same argument runs: the thesis is further along than Q2 shows (BB 1); the foundations blend a strong connected business, with software-grade margins somewhere inside Professional and Consumer and a peer profit pool at Acuity's 24.9 percent Intelligent Spaces margin, with a harvested legacy that Build/Harvest will make visible (BB 2); the January guidance was the rebase (BB 3); the park over-penalises a new team for its predecessors' record, since the red flags, the cuts and the management rating all measure the past three years while the price already discounts them, and the case should progress to Early-Stage work on the connected franchise rather than wait for a print (BB 4).

The record's concessions, at full weight: the price is low and the yield is real and now covered; the cash conversion is real; the cost programme is real and ahead of its timetable; the downgrade cycle is decelerating (one-month revision minus 1 percent, target price unchanged); the Conventional surprise shows the Harvest playbook can work; a trough multiple on a depressed base is where the framework's best setups are found; the actions are real and the price discounts the record. Against the free-cash-flow yield the record notes that the figures are before about EUR 72 million a year of lease payments and before restructuring cash-outs, so the yield to equity after those is nearer 10 to 12 percent than 15 to 16, and that no input gives a profit line for connected lighting, so no cover of enterprise value can be shown.
triggers: - The Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-23 decide the setup either way: a rebased FY2026 range moves the case towards 'Trough on Trough' (passing the guidance condition and probably the estimates-cut and capitulation conditions) at a price nearer EUR 12; a held range with an adjusted EBITA margin at or above 8 percent makes it 'Major Corporate Change' with its first output and re-opens BB 1 at C.

- What would move BB 1 to C: a Q3 print showing the Consumer margin above 5 percent, a reiterated range with a stated second-half bridge, and price-cost at or above zero; what would change our mind on the second half: Q3 adjusted EBITA at or above EUR 115 million (about an 8 percent margin on about EUR 1,440 million of sales) with the range reiterated and a bridge.

- What would change our mind on price-cost: two consecutive quarters with net price-cost at or above zero in the company's bridge. On Consumer: a Q3 Consumer margin above 5 percent with comparable growth positive. On re-rating: two quarters of positive comparable growth with price-cost at zero.
- What would move BB 2 to C: disclosure of Build-portfolio margins standing above 10 percent while the group is at 7.

- Alarm levels: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITA margin below 8.0 percent or guidance language moving to "lower end"; two consecutive quarters of net price-cost at or below minus 90 basis points; Q3 Consumer margin below 4 percent.

- Invalidate levels: FY2026 adjusted EBITA margin below 7.0 percent; Consumer margin still below 4 percent at Q4 2026; a second dividend cut (which would signal terminal decline in Conventional cash flows).
